To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The extent of diversification (as measured by the Herfindahl index) and industry-adjusted levels of capital expenditures are positively related to post-issue operating performance.

the extent of strategic investment choices made by IPO firms at the time of their public offerings is positively related to their post-issue operating performance as well as their ability to remain viable for a longer period of time.
the extent of post-issue diversification and the industry-adjusted capital expenditure intensity are positively related to changes of operating performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of managerial investment decisions at the time of an IPO on the post-issue operating and financial performance and the likelihood of failure of newly public firms.
the following questions: (i) Do strategic investment choices at IPO time affect the subsequent operating performance of newly public US IPO firms?
the impact of strategic decisions on the performance of IPO firms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the long-run, firms that invest heavily in diversification and capital expenditures tend to be more successful in the post-issue period than their counterparts that are not so committed.
the impact of strategic choices on the post-issue operating success and survival of newly public firms is mixed.
“The more a firm diversifies and invests in capital expenditures, the better it does post-IPO and the more likely it is to survive.”
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
firms that invest in product diversification and capital expenditures are able to improve their operating performance and survive longer as public companies.
the strategic investment choices made by IPO issuing firms have important implications for their post-issue operating performance as well as their survival.
diversification and capital investment are important strategic choices that are likely to affect the operating performance and survival of newly public firms in the post-issue period.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extent of managerial commitment to R & D spending and developing diversified lines of business at the time of IPO is a good indicator of a firm's post-issue operating performance.

the extent of pre-issue diversification and capital expenditures are important factors in explaining changes in post-issue operating performance, whereas R&D expenditures are important in explaining the likelihood of failure of newly public firms.

managers of IPO firms should carefully consider the trade-off between the benefits from diversification and R&D investments and the costs associated with the additional resources needed for the execution of such strategies.
